title: Huge Storm Floods New York and New Jersey, Cancels Concerts
summary: What do you call a storm that hits the Northeast with flooding, wind, and canceled concerts? A nor'easter. This weekend, a powerful nor'easter slammed the northeastern U.S., bringing dangerous coastal flooding to New York City, Boston, and New Jersey. States of emergency were declared in New York and New Jersey. In coastal towns like Surf City and Manasquan, streets and homes were underwater. More than 100,000 households lost electricity. Airports were a mess: more than 2,400 flights were delayed and another 1,199 were canceled. Even fun events got washed out. The Red Sox moved their last game against the Chicago Cubs to Sunday in Florida. A professional soccer match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City was canceled. And the Global Citizen Festival in Central Park — which was supposed to feature Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean, and John Legend — was called off. Ed Sheeran's concert at Gillette Stadium near Boston was also canceled. "I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously," Governor Mikie Sherrill said. NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents: "Don't travel if you don't have to. Do not drive or walk through floodwater." Saturday's full moon made the flooding even worse.
why_it_matters: Big storms can shut down power, travel, school, and fun events all in one weekend, so knowing how to stay safe and follow official warnings really matters.

background_read: A nor'easter gets its name because its strongest winds blow in from the northeast along the U.S. East Coast; these storms often hit in fall and winter.
Big coastal storms can push ocean water into city streets — in past storms, flooding has even filled New York City subway tunnels.
Some of the performers whose shows were canceled are famous musicians: Ed Sheeran (a British singer), and Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and John Legend (well-known American singers).
Article_Structure: WHO: Families across the Northeast, Governor Mikie Sherrill of New Jersey, NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani, plus fans of the canceled games and concerts.
WHAT: A powerful nor'easter brought dangerous coastal flooding and wind, knocked out power to more than 100,000 households, and delayed 2,400-plus flights while canceling 1,199.
WHERE: New York City, Boston, New Jersey, and coastal towns like Surf City and Manasquan.
WHY: The storm was dangerous enough that two states declared emergencies and leaders told people not to drive or walk through floodwater.

perspectives.description: They say people should take the storm seriously, stay home, and never walk or drive through floodwater.
People whose flights were delayed or whose concerts and games were canceled lost time, plans, and sometimes money.
They point out that rising seas and high tides like a full moon make coastal flooding worse, so cities need stronger flood defenses.
